Welcome back

How Vox is set up, and your dictations.

Choose your AI provider
Vox needs one AI service for speech and one for cleanup. Pick a provider, get a key from it (most have a free tier or cost very little), paste it below and test it. A server on this PC needs no key.
Hold in any app, speak, then release. Double-tap it to keep listening.

Status

Speed

Measured on this PC and kept only here. Nothing is sent anywhere.

History

Voice notes

Record a quick note: it is written down, tidied up and saved here instead of being pasted into an app. Start it here or from the tray icon and finish it the same way. Esc cancels.

Upcoming

Dictionary

Your own words, names and acronyms. Vox sends them to Whisper as spelling hints and to the cleanup model so they come out right every time.

About you

Who you are, what you work on, how you like to write, terms Vox should know. It is added to every cleanup request so the text comes out your way, so it goes to your cleanup server. While sync is on it is also copied to your relay.

Words

People

Names of people you mention or write to, spelled the way they spell them.

Replacements

When Whisper keeps getting something wrong, force the fix.

Snippets

Say the phrase and Vox types the text you saved, in any app. The text is put in after the AI cleanup, so it never goes to the cleanup server. While sync is on, snippets are copied to your relay. Up to 50, 2,000 characters each.

Recently learned

Fixes Vox picked up when you corrected text it had just typed (Settings, Privacy, Learn from my corrections). Remove takes the fix out of your dictionary again.

Styles

Tone of the cleaned text in each app. Vox detects the app you are typing in.

Default style
Used for apps not listed below.

Settings

Changes apply within a second. No restart needed.

AI providers

AI provider
Vox works with Groq's free tier or any OpenAI-compatible server. Pick one to fill in its address.
Server address
Plain http is only allowed for this PC, your local network and Tailscale.
API key
Stored on this PC (and copied to your relay only if you turn on sharing of API keys under Privacy). A server of your own may not need one.
Voice model
Speech to text. Pick from the list or type a model name.
Cleanup model
Tidies the text. Needs a chat model.
Different server for voice or cleanup
For example Whisper on one machine and Ollama on another. Each server gets only its own key.
Voice server
Address and key for speech to text.
Cleanup server
Address and key for the cleanup model.
Use my relay as the AI server
Speech and text go to your relay, which forwards them to the AI servers set up on its page. Their keys are kept on the relay (in plain text in its relay.json, readable only by its user), so they are not needed here. Fill in the relay address and token under Privacy, Sync between devices.

Voice & audio

Dictation shortcut
Hold to talk and release to insert. Double-tap to keep listening (saves a note); double-tap again to end and save it. Esc cancels a recording or a listening session without sending it.
Note shortcut
Press once to start a voice note that keeps listening, press again to stop and save it. Use Ctrl, Alt or Win plus one letter, digit or F key, for example ctrl+alt+n. Empty turns it off. The keys are not blocked, so the app in front also receives them.
A quick tap of the dictation shortcut
Classic: a tap does nothing (two taps keep listening). Hold or tap: a tap shorter than 0.3 s starts hands-free dictation that runs until you press the shortcut again; holding still means hold to talk, and two taps still keep listening. Esc cancels any recording without sending it.
Hands-free shortcut
Starts hands-free dictation, or ends it and sends what you said. While you hold the dictation shortcut, adding this key keeps the dictation going after you let go. Default ctrl+cmd+space (Ctrl + Win + Space). Empty turns it off.
Paste last dictation
Pastes your last dictation again into the window in front. Default shift+alt+z. Empty turns it off. Like the note shortcut, the keys also reach the app in front.
Copy last dictation
Puts your last dictation on the clipboard, for example shift+alt+x. Empty (the default) turns it off.
Edit by voice (experimental)
Select text, hold these keys and say what to change, for example "make this shorter"; the answer replaces the selection. This sends the selected text and your instruction to your cleanup server. Modifier keys only, for example ctrl+cmd+alt (hold Ctrl + Win, then add Alt). Does not work in terminals. Empty (the default) turns it off.
Microphone
Which microphone Vox listens to. The Windows default unless you pick one. If dictation says it heard nothing, try another.
Language
Auto detect can switch language on short phrases. Pick one to lock it.
Send recordings while I speak
For dictations longer than about 7 seconds, the finished parts are sent to your voice server in pieces at your pauses while you are still talking, so less is left to wait for when you stop. Short recordings are not affected. Uses a few more requests.
Audio format
Automatic sends FLAC (lossless, about half the size of WAV, so it uploads faster) to Groq and OpenAI, and WAV to every other server, your relay included. WAV always sends WAV.
AI cleanup
Removes fillers, applies self-corrections, fixes punctuation and formats lists.
Skip AI cleanup for phrases shorter than N words
Short phrases are pasted as spoken, which is faster. Enter 1 to clean up everything (1 to 20).
Cleanup strength
Light keeps every word you said and only fixes punctuation, capitals, spelling and paragraphs. Standard also removes fillers (um, you know) and false starts. If the cleanup lost words, Vox types your words as spoken instead.
Lists and paragraphs
Auto turns a list you say (first, second; point one, point two; bullet point; pehla, doosra) into a list and starts a new paragraph where you paused for a while in a long dictation. Lists only skips the paragraphs. Off keeps the text flat. Saying commas never makes a list.
Improve my cleanup
Once in a while, a stronger AI model reads your recent dictations (what you said and what Vox typed) and suggests dictionary words, replacements and cleanup rules for you to accept or reject. Nothing is sent until you press Run once and confirm, and nothing changes until you press Apply. Every change can be reverted. About you is only ever suggested to, never changed.
Look at
Model
Runs on , the server used for cleanup. Pick from its model list or type a name. Default openai/gpt-oss-120b.
Tick what you want to keep, then Apply. Unticked items are dropped.
Applied changes
Revert undoes that change and every later one.
Remind me weekly
A message from the tray icon once a week. It only reminds you: it never runs by itself and never sends anything.
Code mode
In the code apps below, and in any app whose style is Code, spoken formatters and symbols become code: camel case user name types userName, open paren types (. No lists are made there. Off types into code apps like into any other app.
Cleanup in code apps
Rules only never sends what you say in a code app to the AI cleanup, so nothing is rewritten. AI cleanup sends it with an instruction to keep identifiers, symbols and casing exactly as spoken.
Code apps
Program names (exe), separated by commas. Common editors and terminals are listed to start with.
What to say in a code app

Say a formatter, then the words: they are joined until you say a symbol, the word then, or stop. Symbols are whole words, so dotted or tabby are never touched. Words in your Dictionary keep their spelling.

Privacy

What leaves this PC: your audio and its transcript go to your voice server, and the cleanup text goes to your cleanup server (both through your relay when it is the AI server). Vox has no analytics and no server of its own.

Keep dictation history
Saves what you dictate on this PC, for the history list. Off means nothing is saved.
Learn from my corrections
Keep dictation on the clipboard
Off by default: after pasting, your earlier copied text comes back. A copied image or file is not restored. On keeps your text copied so you can paste it again with Ctrl + V.
Keep dictations in Windows clipboard history (Win+V)
On by default, so you can pick a dictation again from Win + V. It also means anything you dictate stays in that history until Windows clears it. Off keeps dictations out of Win + V and the cloud clipboard. With it on, dictations still never go to the cloud clipboard.
Sync voice notes with my relay
Keeps your voice notes the same on your phone and PCs through a relay you run yourself (a small server, for example on a Raspberry Pi, reached over Tailscale). While on, the relay receives the full text, raw transcript, tags and device name of each voice note, and your About you text, dictionary, people, snippets, learned cleanup rules, default style, cleanup switch and language. Needs its address and token.
Relay address
For example https://your-pi.your-tailnet.ts.net. Plain http is only allowed for this PC, your local network and Tailscale.
Relay token
Stored only on this PC. Find it in the relay's management page setup or its relay.json.
Also share my provider settings and API keys
Off by default. When on, the AI provider, models and API keys are copied to your other devices through the relay, so anyone with the relay token can read them. Turning this off here removes this device's keys from the relay once. Any other device that still shares keys will put them back, so turn it off on every device.
This device's name
Sent to the relay and shown on its page and on the notes made here. Blank uses the computer name.
About you
Added to every cleanup request, so it goes to your cleanup server. While sync is on it is also copied to your relay. Edit it on the Dictionary page.
How to set up the relay

The relay is a small program that keeps your notes and settings in one place for your phone and PCs. Run it on something that is always on, such as a Raspberry Pi. Tailscale must be installed and signed in on it and on this device, with HTTPS turned on for your tailnet (Tailscale admin console, DNS page).

  1. On the Pi, put relay.py (from the relay folder of Vox) where the service will run it.
    sudo mkdir -p /opt/vox-relay
sudo cp relay.py /opt/vox-relay/
  2. Try it once by hand. It prints where it listens. Stop it with Ctrl+C.
    python3 /opt/vox-relay/relay.py --data-dir /tmp/vox-relay-test --show-token
  3. Install it as a service, so it starts at boot and restarts if it stops (vox-relay.service is next to relay.py).
    sudo cp vox-relay.service /etc/systemd/system/
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now vox-relay
  4. Read the token. Keep it private: anyone with the token and a way to reach the relay can read your notes.
    sudo cat /var/lib/vox-relay/relay.json
  5. Publish it to your tailnet. This is what adds HTTPS. Never use tailscale funnel, which puts it on the open internet. The second command shows the address.
    sudo tailscale serve --bg 8765
tailscale serve status
  6. Enter that address (like https://your-pi.your-tailnet.ts.net) and the token in the fields above, then press Test connection. It tells you whether the relay is reachable, whether the token works, and the name this device shows under.

No Raspberry Pi? A Windows PC can run it: in the Vox tray menu tick Run relay on this PC, then run tailscale serve --bg 8765 in a terminal. It only works while that PC is on and Vox is running.

Devices on my relay
Phones and PCs that have used your relay, newest first, as the relay itself recorded them. Needs the relay address and token above; the only thing sent from here is this device's name.
